::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 21st 1874  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: Ms. Eng. lett. e.116 ff 172-3.[^1]
:::

My dear [Miss Palmer](people/person_1238.qmd)
I enclose the order. I wrote Hants after Sep upon the paper, so I hope they made it out to the right one It will be a great pleasure to me to come to Blackmoor [erasure] Thank [Lady Selborne](people/person_2299.qmd) for her kind invitation.[^2]

What would suit me best would be to come when I leave Crookham, on the 3d or 4th of September, as then I could take the train at Alton and go home from you instead of back to Crookham Would this be convenient to Lady Selborne?

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Envelope addressed to 'The Honble/ Laura Palmer/ Blackmoor,/ Petersfield,' postmarked 'Winchester/JY/ 21/74'.
[^2]: Laura Palmer’s mother, born Lady Laura Waldegrave (d 10 April 1885), who had married (1848)  Roundell Palmer, created  (1872)  Lord Selborne and (1882) Earl of Selborne.
